Many people assume that Big Bitcoin is maliciously designing narratives behind the scenes.

This is not what happens.

In fact, I think you can look to your own life for examples of the psychological dynamic at play here.

Something happens, and you assign a story about yourself.

“Nobody understands me, and it's because there’s something wrong with me.”

You build an identity around what happened to you, and you move forward with that identity.

Over time (if you're someone who grows and adapts your mindset to new information) you may realize the identity you once gave yourself no longer rings true.

You choose to tell yourself a different story (hopefully a positive one).

“There is nothing wrong with me at all. People just didn't understand me because I was doing something unusual.”

You may even adopt a new identity.

You adapt to new narratives and stories to define who you are.

"I'm somebody who does unique things."

This exact same dynamic happens in the broader Bitcoin market.

Narratives come.

Narratives go.

Narratives shift and change as new entries come into the market and new things sound like more persuasive reasons to buy the orange coin.

Bitcoin was:

1) Electronic cash
2) Censorship-resistant money
3) Digital gold
4) An inflation hedge
5) An institutional asset

None of these narratives came about because a room full of people decided what Bitcoin should become next.

Narratives emerge.

People holding Bitcoin are constantly trying to explain (to themselves and everyone else) what this thing is and why it matters.

Bitcoin's monetary properties do not change.

But the world and the people around it change CONSTANTLY. And every time the world changes, people find new reasons those same properties matter.

The next bullish Bitcoin narrative is out there right now.

Only time will tell how long it takes to be discovered.

BREAKING: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries dropped -$72 billion in June, to $9.30 trillion, to the lowest level since January.

This marks the 3rd monthly decline over the last 4 months, totaling -$190 billion.

Japan, the largest foreign holder, reduced its holdings by -$26 billion in June, to $1.12 trillion, the lowest since January 2025.

The UK, the 2nd-largest holder, cut its holdings by -$9 billion, to $940 billion, the 2nd-largest on record.

China, the 3rd-largest holder, trimmed its holdings by -$26 billion, to $633 billion, the lowest since September 2008.

Meanwhile, foreign official holders, such as central banks and government entities, reduced their Treasury holdings by -$70 billion in June, to $3.78 trillion, the lowest since February 2024.

Foreign demand for US Treasuries is losing momentum.

Foreign investors outside the US purchased +$181.4 billion of US equities in June.

The private sector alone bought a record +$144.7 billion, bringing an annualized rate to +$1.74 trillion, an all-time high.

Over the past 3 months, private purchases have totaled +$351.1 billion, equivalent to an annualized pace of +$1.4 trillion, also an all-time high.

This surpasses the 2025 annualized record by ~$400.0 billion.

By comparison, foreign official institutions, such as central banks and sovereign wealth funds, purchased +$36.7 billion in June.

As a result, private investors accounted for ~80% of all foreign equity purchases over this period.

The appetite for US stocks is stronger than ever.

There are many things kid analysts got wrong. They failed to recognize the lack of a business cycle. They failed to understand the reasons behind Bitcoin’s compressed volatility. Most importantly, there can be no bear market if there was no bull market. Now the cycle completes.

BTC is an community based energy asset that historically accelerates out of bear markets when vol has compressed and it is ignored.  This is measured best in sigma moves. The pattern of the last two major shifts coming out of 2018 and 2022 (I hate to say four year cycle but yes) the pattern was seen by a large weekly sigma move where BTC crossed the 200 day moving average the week of the sigma move.  So far this week is exactly the same pattern.  More in this week's video.

The 4 year cycle bear market simpletons were wrong. Markets are never that simple. They are deeply complex puzzles that require deeper thought to crack over any period of time. Consider it a lesson learned. Not everyone deserves to be a billionaire. Enjoy this half of the cycle.
